---
title: "Run a server"
guide-section: How-to guides
---

A server shares one directory of DAS files, with [rules](32-access.qmd) saying who may read each file.

## Make a key for each user

```bash
dastor new-key
```

It prints:

```text
key:        <give this to the user>
key_sha256: <put this in the config>
```

Only the digest goes in the config. `dastor hash-key` prints the digest of a key you already have, read from stdin.

## Write a config

```yaml
spool:
  path: /data/das               # a directory of DAS files, indexed recursively
  refresh_seconds: 300          # re-index every 5 minutes
  rules:
    - column: tag
      pattern: "^public"
      allow: ["*"]              # everyone, including visitors
    - column: source_path       # paths are relative to the directory
      pattern: "^project_a/"
      allow: ["group:lab"]
users:
  - name: alice
    key_sha256: <digest from dastor new-key>
    groups: [lab]
annotations:                    # optional: turns on annotations
  path: /data/das_annotations   # a directory outside the data directory
```

[Configuration](41-config.qmd) lists every key.

## Start it

```bash
dastor serve config.yaml --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

The server runs as one process. It indexes the directory at start, and again every `refresh_seconds`, and loads patches in a thread pool. The viewer is at `/viewer/`; users sign in there with their key.

## Let only users in

Leave `*` out of every rule. Visitors are then turned away before any work: the API answers them 401, and the viewer sends them to `/signin`.

## Serve it on the internet

[Put it behind a reverse proxy](13-proxy.qmd), which ends TLS and limits how often clients may ask.
